Episode 251: The Great Adversaries (10)
“Lady Lucy, if I’m correct, your eldest daughter is currently...Captured by Rokia Ganesto.”
“Captured is perhaps not the right word. One day, she left me of her own accord to seek Rokia.”
“She left on her own? To Rokia?”

“Yes. At that time, I still had my power as a Knight, but Heilyn easily overpowered me and said... she needed Rokia. It was during winter, when Heilyn was eight years old. We were living on an uninhabited island of the empire.”
Throughout their exile, Lucy never mentioned anything about her family. She lived abandoning even the name ‘Runkandel’, using an alias and, of course, her daughters didn't know their true lineage.
“Before leaving me in shock, Heilyn subsumed the entire island into a sub-space. It was a sub-space for forsaken, exiled dragons. She imprisoned me there.”
Exiled dragons.
According to Lucy, 'special dragons' forsaken by the gods were all discarded in the same sub-space.
Gods cannot kill dragons too closely linked to their own powers, as their death weakens them. So instead of killing, gods exiled dragons to sub-spaces, never opened again until Heilyn did.
The somewhat clumsy dragons in the Ice Castle were the descendants of those exiled dragons.
“Wait, perhaps your daughter was placing you in a safe place? You survived almost a thousand years in that sub-space. Heilyn might have been aware of her powers from the beginning, unlike you.”

Heilyn had never mentioned Rokia but suddenly said she needed her and, despite not teaching her any magic beyond basic swordsmanship, opened a divine power sub-space. As Talaris suggested, Heilyn might have known her powers from the start.

“...I’ve considered that, Lady Talarris. As a head of the great serpent, I adapted well to that world. However, currently, Rokia is pursuing me. Joshua Runkandel. No, now Joshua Ganesto. He came looking for me.”
Hearing Joshua's name, Jin pressed his forehead.
Lucy recounted her battles with Joshua in the exiled space. Joshua, empowered by Rokia, demonstrated significant combat prowess but couldn’t inflict any fundamental harm on Lucy.
“That insect-like fellow... never dies and keeps causing trouble. It's disgraceful.”

“It’s not something you need to apologize for, Lord. After all, he's just a moth unaware of anything. He thinks of Rokia as his new mother, but for Rokia, he is nothing more than a disposable tool. A means to an end.”
Considering Rokia's goal, Jin narrowed his eyes.
“From my deductions, Rokia seems to be trying to create... her own paradise.”

“That's correct, Lord Jin. She has already created her world where she reigns as the sole deity. According to Joshua, in that world, the Runkandels won the Sword-Demon War against Ziffle. He claims that's how history should have rightfully unfolded.”
Jin was reminded of something Luke had told him about.
Luke’s reason for reviving the Sun God was to establish a world where the Plutonians eternally triumph, similar in many ways to Rokia’s world.
“She wants to replace the current world with her peculiar one, Rokia does.”
Perhaps she intends to replace not just one world.

Suddenly, Jin had that thought. If Rokia knew about the multiverse, either recently like Jin or even earlier, her plan might involve transforming all dimensions into ‘worlds where the Runkandels win’.
Jin shared his sudden conjecture with Lucy, along with explaining the concept of the multiverse. Hearing this, Lucy’s eyes widened in realization.
“The multiverse... Oh, then what Heilyn said when she left... could have meant that.”
- To destroy all worlds, I need Rokia Ganesto. You and Makos stay here.
The words Heilyn left when departing from Lucy.

Lucy had pondered those words for a thousand years, interpreting them as metaphorical for the complete destruction of this world. However, if Heilyn was aware of the multiverse from that point, the meaning changes completely.
Heilyn might literally desire the 'end of all dimensions.' As the group contemplated this, they felt a chill run down their spines.

"…When I confronted Rokia recently, I saw her with a face resembling Themar's. Discussing with Murakan, I pondered the possibility of a child between Themar and Lady Lucy, and considered that Rokia might have seized one of their bodies."
"That must be Heilyn's body."
"When Rokia revealed herself… it's a bit uncomfortable for me to keep calling her your daughter, Lady Lucy, since she is an ancestor to me. I'll refer to her as Lady Heilyn."
"Ahaha, Jin, you're funny at times like this. Then why do you casually call Themar by his name?"

"I guess I've gotten used to it. There's a strange familiarity with the first head of the family. Anyway, I didn't sense any of Lady Heilyn’s consciousness or will in Rokia. She seemed to be purely herself."
That's why Jin had previously thought Rokia was exploiting the body of Themar and Lucy's child.
However, it could be the other way around. Perhaps, Heilyn was using Rokia.
Jin couldn't bring himself to voice this to Lucy, but she seemed to have already guessed it and nodded solemnly.
"Whether Rokia is using Heilyn or Heilyn is using Rokia... either way, it's a terrible ordeal for our family and the world."
Lucy paused, recalling the days she spent fleeing with her daughters a thousand years ago.
Heilyn, an almost emotionless child, would occasionally hold Lucy’s hand when she was distressed.

Despite the lack of such memories, Heilyn and Makos were Lucy's most precious daughters. But one of them turned out to be a being intent on destroying this world and all dimensions, using power inherited from herself.
Even after a thousand years, it was a hard truth to accept.
But it was an unavoidable reality.

"We must stop Heilyn, one way or another. Only then she can be freed from the will of destruction. Lord. I am a person whose very existence is a sin. Despite being an unspeakably dreadful being from birth, despite only realizing my true nature belatedly, I still want to fight."
Tears streamed down Lucy's expressionless face.
She lost her family, colleagues, lover, children, and even herself. Incomprehensible agony led her to curse the world, the Sun God, the gods, her enemies, and herself.
Yet she never gave up on life, meaning she never ceased her struggle.

"Please don't say that….., Lady Lucy. Everyone who survived owes a debt to Runkandel of that time, and I am the biggest beneficiary. The person before me now is not the head of Ameris or a fragment of the Sun God, but the Ten Swords Knight, Lucy Runkandel, who never stopped fighting. It's an honor to fight alongside you."

Wiping her tears, Lucy nodded. Her golden eyes, filled with profound void, sorrow, and rage towards her enemies, reflected a madness that couldn't be overshadowed by the void and sorrow tormenting her for a millennium.
"Both the family and the alliance will welcome you, Lady Lucy. Many will be especially glad to see you."
"Manor Lord, may I accompany the Lord to meet old friends and now comrades?"
"Huh? Why ask that? You're my guest, not a subordinate. Technically, you're even my senior, but let's just be friends. I've liked you from the start. That's why we had a massage together."
"If I can share friendship with someone who is sin itself..."

"Enough of that sin talk. Did all that happen because you wanted it? You're just a victim of the world, like many others. As my son-in-law said, it's rather the people of the world who owe you. You were so frustratingly modest during the massage, I'm going crazy."
Jin informed the Sword Garden and Tikan of the situation via communicator. The Golden Fleet had just finished off the remnants of the Sun God religion. To honor Lucy, Jin called the Golden Fleet.
"Lady Talaris , I'll escort Lady Lucy back. Would you like to join us?"
"I'll pass. I have to play with the dragon brothers Lucy brought. Daughter, are you coming?"
"I have some paperwork to catch up on, Jin. Lady Lucy, we'll be seeing each other often from now on, so I look forward to working with you."
Soon after, the Golden Fleet arrived and took Jin and Lucy aboard. Talaris and Siris saw them off.
"Huh? Daughter, you braided your hair differently than usual? Hehe, it's beautiful. You're my daughter, but you're truly gorgeous."
"Is that so?"
Talarris looked at Siris in surprise. Usually, Syris ignored her mother's playful affections.
"Why the response? Feeling good after being with your husband?"
To that, Siris calmly replied.
"If mother says it's pretty, then I should wear it like this from now on."
